decision_note: Primary Solidago study links herbivory and floral volatile phenotype to pollination success and seed production in a natural population; retain for source-level shared-coordinate adjudication.
Primary Vaccinium study jointly evaluates flowering schedule, pollination, flower/seed predation and fruit production across subpopulations and years; retain.
Dissertation explicitly centers floral mutualists, antagonists and consequences for plant reproduction; retain for chapter-level primary-source and independence adjudication.

Primary tropical-shrub study links light-driven floral-trait variation, nectar robbery and reproductive output through multiple pathways; retain under TA uncertainty for pollinator/antagonist source coding.

Abronia thesis directly studies attractive floral traits, moth pollination and low seed set; registered query context suggests possible additional antagonistic channels, so TA uncertainty resolves to full-text retention.
Primary Desfontainia experiment compares legitimate pollination, nectar robbery and seed production while quantifying floral rewards and visitor behaviour; retain.
Primary Lonicera study experimentally evaluates nectar robbers as pollinators, effects on legitimate visitors, and plant reproduction; retain for role-boundary adjudication.
Primary Ipomopsis experiment manipulates nectar-robbing intensity and measures pollen-transfer and multiple plant-fitness components; retain.
Primary Tirpitzia study quantifies nectar robbery, pollinator behaviour and male/female reproductive fitness across floral morphs; retain.
Primary Sesamum study compares robbed and unrobbed flowers, legitimate/robbing pollinator behaviour and seed set; retain for dual-role coding.
Primary Tecomella study experimentally manipulates nectar robbery and measures pollinator foraging and reproductive success; retain.
Primary elevational Clinopodium study jointly measures legitimate pollinator availability, nectar robbing and seed production; retain for spatial interaction-context adjudication.
Published primary Digitalis study quantifies novel nectar robbery, floral visitor context and reproductive output; retain.
Preprint/report identity of the Digitalis nectar-robbing study; retain at TA stage and resolve duplicate-report status at full text.
Primary Lonicera study measures aphid herbivory effects on floral morphology/rewards, pollination and fruit/seed production; retain.
Primary Brassica nigra experiment crosses herbivore identity and plant ontogenetic context and measures flower-visitor interactions plus seed fitness; retain for source-design adjudication.
Primary Iris experiment manipulates florivore exposure, documents pollinator-to-robber role shifts and measures reproductive success; retain.
Primary Primula study relates soil-moisture context to nectar robbing, pollinator interaction pathways and plant fitness; retain.
Primary Salvia study quantifies spatiotemporal nectar robbery, floral visitation/pollen deposition and seed set across populations and years; retain.
Focused meta-analysis of floral larceny effects on flower traits, pollinator visitation and plant reproductive success; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material, not as a primary study.
Passiflora study relates style-deflexion mean/variability to pollination and fitness traits under natural pollination; no focal plant antagonist/exploiter component is evaluated.
Avocado nectar-microbiota study assays plant and honeybee pathogens plus microbial effects on model-plant growth, but does not measure a focal pollinator response/service to the floral coordinate.

Primary Brassica incana study spans an urbanization gradient and jointly measures pollinator community, herbivore damage, phenotypic traits and reproductive success; retain for spatial/context source adjudication.
